report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of correctness.py: digest, freeze_selection, _check_selection, BeforeState, judge_before_state, CorrectnessResult, judge_after_state, _run_lists. Claims verified; several docstring claims are uncheckable within this chunk.
risks: _run_lists | medium | If the f2p run succeeds but p2p invocation fails, p2p statuses are empty; the code returns empty p2p without recording an error, potentially leading to a false 'fixed' verdict. The docstring claims collection errors abort the whole invocation, but the code doesn't handle that case explicitly. | Inspect the TestRunner contract outside this chunk to see if exceptions propagate or are caught.

handoff.purpose: Defines selection digest, freeze_selection, _check_selection guard, BeforeState, judge_before_state, CorrectnessResult, judge_after_state, and _run_lists.

symbols.name: digest
symbols.note: Property on Selection; returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of canonical JSON of selection fields.

symbols.name: freeze_selection
symbols.note: Creates immutable Selection from task dict; deduplicates and sorts node lists; fixes gate to 'pytest'.

symbols.name: _check_selection
symbols.note: Guard comparing observed vs declared node sets; returns error string if extra or missing nodes.

symbols.name: BeforeState
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding before-state verification result and reasons.

symbols.name: BeforeState.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes BeforeState to dict, including selection and its digest.

symbols.name: judge_before_state
symbols.note: Pure function converting before-state statuses into BeforeState verdict with ordered refusals.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding one evaluation outcome and supporting data.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult.ok
symbols.note: Returns True only when outcome == OUTCOME_FIXED.

symbols.name: judge_after_state
symbols.note: Pure function determining outcome and node lists after a change.

symbols.name: _run_lists
symbols.note: Runs FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as separate invocations using the frozen selection.

claims.text: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem.
claims.why: The function uses dict.fromkeys and sorted on the raw list values from the task dict; no expansion, filtering, or filesystem access is performed.

claims.text: There is deliberately no pattern, glob or directory walk here: a set that could grow to match something a candidate added is not a frozen set, and this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: The first part is kept (no pattern/glob/walk in this function), but the claim that this is the only place a set is built for an evaluation cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: GUARD: the run reported on EXACTLY the frozen nodes, or say what moved.
claims.why: The function compares observed and declared sets and returns an error string if there are extra or missing nodes.

claims.text: A runner is injectable, and a gate is a subprocess whose output is parsed; either could in principle report a node that is not in the frozen set (a parser that matched too loosely, a runner that expanded a selector).
claims.why: The injectable runner and gate subprocess are not visible in this chunk; the claim about their behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: A result computed over a set that is not the declared one is not the measurement that was declared, so it is refused rather than reported.
claims.why: The function returns an error string, but whether that error is used to refuse the result is determined by callers outside this chunk.

claims.text: ``verified`` is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed.
claims.why: The dataclass does not enforce this; it is a description of how the field is set by judge_before_state, which is in this chunk but the constants PROVEN_NOT_PASSING and STATUS_PASSED are defined elsewhere.

claims.text: Anything else is either an invalid task or an unobtainable verdict, and ``reasons`` says which.
claims.why: The docstring describes the semantics of the fields; the actual assignment logic is in judge_before_state, but the constants used there are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Pure: turn before-state node statuses into a verdict about the TASK.
claims.why: The function has no side effects; it only reads inputs and returns a new BeforeState.

claims.text: 1. NO VERDICT (``not_run``) -> ``unrunnable``. An unknown never becomes a fact in either direction.
claims.why: The function checks for nodes in NO_VERDICT and returns unrunnable=True, but NO_VERDICT is defined elsewhere; the claim that 'not_run' is in NO_VERDICT cannot be verified here.

claims.text: 2. A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> ``invalid``.
claims.why: The function marks invalid for any f2p status not in PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, which includes PASSED, SKIPPED, and MISSING, but PROVEN_NOT_PASSING is defined elsewhere.

claims.text: 3. A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> ``invalid``.
claims.why: The function marks invalid for any p2p status != STATUS_PASSED, but STATUS_PASSED is defined elsewhere.

claims.text: Pure: ``(outcome, reason, fixed, unfixed, regressed)`` after the change.
claims.why: The function is pure; it returns a tuple of outcome, reason, and three node tuples without side effects.

claims.text: ``could_not_run`` first, because an unattributed node is an unknown and an unknown must never be read as a verdict.
claims.why: The function checks for unknown nodes first and returns OUTCOME_COULD_NOT_RUN if any exist.

claims.text: ``regressed`` next, because a change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green -- collapsing those two into one boolean is exactly how a plausible-looking bad patch gets promoted.
claims.why: The function computes regressed and returns OUTCOME_REGRESSED before checking unfixed, so a regression takes precedence over fixed.

claims.text: Takes the frozen :class:`Selection`, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule: once a selection is frozen there is no code path left that can consult the task for node ids again, so a task mutated mid-evaluation (by a runner, a gate, or a caller holding the same dict) cannot change what is measured.
claims.why: The function does take a Selection and uses its node lists, but the claim that no code path can consult the task again is a global property that cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into ``not_run`` (measured -- one uncollectable node id aborts the whole invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs).
claims.why: The function does run f2p and p2p separately, but the behavior on collection errors (exit code 4) depends on the runner implementation, which is not in this chunk.

observations.what: The docstring for _run_lists claims that a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into not_run, but the code does not handle the case where the f2p run fails: it would raise an exception and the function would not return, or if the runner catches errors internally, the p2p statuses might be empty. The code does not explicitly check for errors.

The docstring for judge_before_state implies that NO_VERDICT includes 'not_run', but the actual constant is defined elsewhere. The code checks membership in NO_VERDICT, but the exact set is not visible.

The digest property is deterministic and uses a canonical JSON serialization, but the selection fields are not all included (e.g., base_revision is included, but the property is on Selection and includes all fields in the JSON). The digest is truncated to 16 hex chars, which is a potential collision risk but not a correctness issue.
